transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-12
Start: 15:00 PT
Scheduled: 1h
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jamal Ortiz (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Lina Chen (Suncrest Head of AI), Marco Silva (Platform Eng), Ravi Kapoor (InfoSec), Sofia Alvarez (Product PM)

Auto-generated summary (optional):
Suncrest is scoping a POC to validate latency SLOs and cost for a customer-facing prompt-answering feature. Primary objectives: define success criteria, gather workload telemetry (QPS, concurrency, token distribution), design benchmark playbook and replay plan. Security constraints discussed (VPC/private deployment, audit logs). Next step: share benchmark playbook and traffic replay scripts; customer to provide 7-day traces and prompt sample.

Topics:
- Workload fingerprinting: QPS peaks, concurrency, burst patterns
- Token distribution: input/output length buckets, streaming vs non-streaming
- Benchmark design: models to test, quantization, warm/cache assumptions
- Deployment constraints: VPC, KMS, SOC2 artifacts
Action items and next steps: covered at end

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jamal: all right hello everyone thanks for joining, this is Jamal from Redwood, i'm joined by priya our se, and we are here to run through the poc traffic fingerprint and a benchmarking playbook. um Lina, do you want to kick off with a quick summary of the feature you want to validate?
[00:12] Lina: yeah sure, thanks jamal. so we're rolling out a customer support summarization and answer assistant for our renewables customer portal. goal is sub-300ms median and sub-500ms p95 for single-turn queries, but we also need to understand cost per 1k requests. the traffic is pretty bursty around morning reports and incident windows.
[00:29] Marco: quick add, traffic comes from edge proxies, we have sudden bursts when telemetry pumps in after batch jobs. average concurrent sessions right now is about 30, but peaks hit 300 for 10-15 minutes.
[00:39] Priya: okay that's helpful. do you have sample telemetry in a form we can replay? like request timestamps, prompt lengths, token counts? even approximate histograms help.
[00:47] Lina: we can export logs, yes. we typically keep 30 days, we can slice a 7-day sample. we'll need to scrub PII though.
[00:54] Ravi: on the security side, we are only allowed to provide anonymized request bodies; storage needs to be inside our VPC or with customer-managed keys. can you outline options for a private deployment?
[01:03] Jamal: absolutely, we support hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC/on-prem). for the POC we can run the replay against a private instance in your VPC or a Redwood-dedicated tenancy depending on your preference and allowed data flows. we'll include an options matrix in the playbook.
[01:18] Sofia: timeline question — how long does a typical benchmark take? we have a release gate scheduled july 15th.
[01:24] Priya: depends on scope — a full sweep (mult models, quant profiles, multiple sequence-length buckets) often runs 24-72 hours of continuous replay to capture tails. but an initial baseline run for p95/p99 on a representative day can be 4-6 hours.
[01:36] Marco: can you be specific about what you need from our end for the 4-6 hour baseline?
[01:40] Priya: ideally a 24-hour compressed trace or a 7-day sample from which we pick representative hours. also the top 500 prompts and an idea of prompt templates that are latency-sensitive. we also need concurrency shaping config — e.g., ramp profiles.
[01:52] Lina: got it. we can do 7 days and pick peaks.
[01:56] Jamal: let's talk metrics. typically we measure: median latency, p95, p99, tokens-per-request (in/out), throughput (QPS), and cost per 1k responses given subscription/instance footprint. does that align with your success metrics?
[02:09] Sofia: yes cost per 1k and p95 are our primary. also reliability — percent of requests that hit fallback (we have a cached answer fallback).
[02:17] Ravi: and auditability — we need request-level logs for any security incident and KMS-managed keys for model encryption.
[02:24] Priya: note on caching: if you have a high prefix overlap, prefix/KV caching can reduce compute significantly. we need to know cache hit expectations during replay — are these mostly unique customer queries or repeated templates?
[02:36] Marco: about 60% template-based with variable data points; maybe 40% unique free-text. so we expect modest prefix reuse.
[02:44] Jamal: that's good — we'll include cache-on and cache-off runs in the playbook.

[03:00] [Timestamp jump: 03:00] Priya: onto token distribution. do you have distributions for input length and response length? we typically bucket into short (0-64 tokens), medium (65-256), long (257-1024), and episodic (>1024).
[03:12] Lina: most user queries are short to medium, about 70% under 256 input tokens. outputs vary: 50% under 128, 30% 128-512, rest longer when it's a full incident summary.
[03:24] Priya: good — so for benchmarks we'll run sequences with output length target buckets: 64, 256, 512 and a few >1k to exercise kvcache. also stream vs non-stream — do you stream responses to the client today?
[03:36] Sofia: yes we stream for long answers in product, so the streaming latency tail matters.
[03:41] Jamal: streaming changes the latency profile because you can push initial tokens faster; we'll measure TTF (time-to-first-token) and TTA (time-to-all-tokens) as separate KPIs.

[03:58] Marco: about concurrency — can you emulate user think-times and session stickiness? because our load is not uniform.
[04:05] Priya: yes, replay tool supports stochastic arrival processes, think-time distributions, and sticky sessions. send us the session length distribution and we can craft a playback with similar inter-arrival times.
[04:14] Marco: we'll provide the session traces.

[04:28] [04:28] Ravi: one more on deployments — if we do private deployment, what's the process to run benchmarks in our environment? do you ship an appliance or a container?
[04:36] Jamal: we provide a private control plane and a runtime bundle. options: (1) Redwood-managed inside your VPC with customer-managed KMS keys; (2) fully customer-run where we give an on-prem package and support; (3) dedicated tenancy in Redwood cloud with VPC peering. the playbook will detail the tradeoffs.
[04:50] Ravi: we prefer option 1 or 2, leaning toward fully managed in our VPC. need to validate that keys never leave KMS.

[05:02] Priya: noted. security checks we'll include — SOC2 artifacts, encryption at rest/in transit, audit log format, retention windows.

[05:10] Jamal: back to benchmarks — models. do you have a preference for open models or do you plan to run proprietary fine-tuned models?
[05:17] Lina: we are evaluating both. primary proof should use our in-house fine-tuned model (we can export a weights snapshot) but we'd like Redwood to provide an open-model baseline to compare cost & latency.
[05:27] Priya: ok we usually test 3 configs: open baseline (e.g., a community LLM), fine-tuned customer model, and a quantized variant of the customer model (int8/4). that way we can estimate delta in latency and quality.
[05:38] Marco: for GPU sizing — any rule-of-thumb mapping QPS to GPU count? our projected steady QPS is 12, peaks 300.
[05:47] Priya: rough mapping depends on model size and sequence length; for example a 13B model at 256 token average might do around 15-25 qps per A100-like GPU with kv cache warmed, but with batching and lower precision you can push higher. we'll provide a capacity table in the playbook.
[06:01] Jamal: also we recommend testing continuous batching and burst handling — there are policies that trade slightly higher median for much better tail.

[06:12] [06:12] Sofia: how do you measure cost per 1k? do you include infra amortized or just Redwood unit pricing?
[06:18] Jamal: we'll show both: unit compute cost (infra) and an end-to-end cost per 1k including networking and cache savings under different caching/batching setups.

[06:30] Priya: quality checks — how will you do regression tests for response quality? are we evaluating with eval sets or human raters?
[06:37] Lina: we'd like automated evals on our classification metrics and a human spot-check for a sample of top 100 prompts.
[06:43] Priya: we'll bake that into the playbook: automated BLEU/ROUGE-like checks where applicable, and a small human review for hallucination checks.

[06:56] [06:56] Marco: real quick — what about warm vs cold cache experiments? how are those handled?
[07:01] Priya: we run three scenarios: cold start (empty KV/memory), warm cache (primed using a preload phase), and steady-state (long-running with realistic cache eviction). each run is documented with how we prime and what metrics to capture.

[07:12] Jamal: i'm going to share a high-level playbook now (we'll send the doc after the call). it includes: objectives, required artifacts from customer, replay tool config examples, model matrix, run schedule (baseline, scale, stress), metrics dashboard templates, and a decision rubric for rollout.
[07:28] Lina: please add a checklist for privacy scrubbing and sample approval before Redwood ingests data.
[07:34] Jamal: yes we'll add that.

[07:40] [07:40] Sofia: can you walk through an example run in the playbook? like step-by-step for a 6-hour baseline.
[07:46] Priya: sure. step 0: dataset ingest and scrub. step 1: pick representative hour(s) and replay at matching arrival rates with session stickiness. step 2: run against 3 model configs: open baseline, tuned, quantized tuned. step 3: capture TTF/TTA, p50/p95/p99, QPS, token metrics, fallback rate. step 4: do cache-on and cache-off runs. step 5: run a 30-minute stress at peak QPS to see graceful degradation. step 6: aggregate and produce dashboard.
[08:12] Marco: that stress test — do you do graceful fallback to cheaper model or queued requests?
[08:17] Priya: yes we simulate routing policies: fallback to smaller model, regional reroute, and queue with soft-timeout. we capture user-visible error rates for each policy.

[08:28] [08:28] Ravi: retention and audit logs — do you keep logs for the benchmark run? if so, can we keep them inside our S3 with our KMS?
[08:35] Jamal: yes, logs can be exported to your S3 with your KMS, or Redwood can host and give you access with strict retention windows. we'll include both options in the doc.

[08:45] Lina: what about data minimization — can we replay fingerprints instead of full payloads?
[08:50] Priya: you can supply hashed/pseudonymized inputs and synthetic payloads that preserve token-length distribution. both work to validate performance; to test quality we'll need raw or partially anonymized text for a small sample.

[09:02] [09:02] Jamal: a couple of gotchas we often see: (1) mixing streaming and non-streaming runs without switching client expectations causes misleading p95, (2) not priming kv cache for template-heavy workloads dramatically underestimates cost savings, (3) sending production traffic with high variance but testing only steady QPS underestimates tail. we'll document these.

[09:22] Sofia: do you have an example benchmark artifact we can look at?
[09:26] Jamal: yes, we'll share a sample playbook and a reference spreadsheet with config and expected outputs. link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/sample-playbook (note: internal link)

[09:38] [09:38] Marco: for benchmarks, what observability do we get? traces, per-token cost breakdown, per-route latency?
[09:45] Priya: full traces, token-level cost breakdown, model-level dashboards, and error analysis. we also produce a run-book that ties metrics to recommended instance counts.

[09:56] Lina: i'm worried about the p99 tail — our SLA is strict on p99. how do you size for p99?
[10:02] Priya: we size primarily by testing with realistic burst profiles and ensuring we have headroom: overprovisioning strategy, autoscale thresholds, and fallback policies. we'll generate sizing tables showing the probability of p99 breaches under different provisioning.

[10:16] [10:16] Jamal: to make sure we're aligned, can we confirm success criteria right now? Lina?
[10:20] Lina: yes — success = (1) p95 < 500ms and p99 < 1200ms for the defined 90% typical traffic, (2) cost per 1k responses within target range (we'll share number offline), (3) no security or key leakage in private deployment trial, (4) clear rollout recipe for production.
[10:36] Jamal: okay noted. we'll include those as acceptance criteria in the playbook.

[10:42] [10:42] Priya: a quick question on measuring p99 — do you want absolute wall-clock p99 or p99 under percentile of tokens (like p99 initial token)?
[10:50] Sofia: both ideally — TTF p99 and overall p99.

[10:56] [10:56] Marco: about the replay tool — does it preserve header metadata and auth tokens? we can't share real auth tokens.
[11:03] Priya: we don't need auth tokens; the replay tool mimics header sizes and shapes, you can provide token-length placeholders.

[11:12] [11:12] Jamal: last operational note — we will run an initial lightweight run in Redwood hosted infra first to get a baseline within 48 hours of receiving data, then move to private VPC runs as soon as infra is provisioned.

[11:24] Ravi: that sequence sounds fine. one ask: please provide a small compliance questionnaire we can give our auditors.
[11:30] Jamal: we'll attach a security packet and SOC2 summary with the playbook.

[11:36] [11:36] Sofia: ok great. recap?
[11:38] Jamal: recap: Redwood to send benchmark playbook + sample replay scripts; Priya to draft baseline benchmark config; Suncrest to deliver 7-day anonymized traffic and top prompts; schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2026-06-22; security packet will be shared.
[11:53] Lina: confirm i'll review with infra and sec.
[11:56] Marco: i'll own the telemetry export.
[11:58] Ravi: i'll review the compliance questionnaire.
[12:00] Jamal: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with docs and calendar invite for kickoff.

End of transcript.
